newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury resumes deliberations with new member.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury resumes deliberations with new member.

text.p: The newly reconstituted jury in O.J. Simpson's civil trial began its first full day of deliberations on Monday with no indication of when a verdict would be reached.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki ordered jurors to start all over on Friday after he removed the panel's only black member and replaced her with an alternate. The original panel considered the case for about 14 hours over three days last week.

Juror Rosemary Caraway was removed after Fujisaki learned she had failed to disclose that her daughter worked in the Los Angeles County District Attorney's office. She was replaced by an Asian man in his 30s who works as a computer programmer.
The six-woman, six-man jury now includes nine whites, one Asian, one Hispanic and one man who is part-black, part-Asian.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, in October 1995. He is fighting a wrongful-death lawsuit filed by the victims' families, who are seeking substantial damages.
A court spokeswoman said Fujisaki had set a hearing on Monday at the request of Simpson's lead defence attorney, Robert Baker. The subject was not immediately known.
In another development, CNN reported that Simpson had denied a report in Monday's New York Post that he had held a Pro Bowl football game party at his mansion on Sunday.

Headlined "O.J. Parties as His Trial Falls Apart," the Post story said Simpson, a former football star, was in a "celebratory mood" at a party for the National Football League's all-star game that "rocked on for hours."

And the March issue of Playboy featured a nude spread of Nicole Brown Simpson's friend, Faye Resnick, who wrote a best-selling book about the slain woman's life shortly after the killings. Simpson has suggested in several interviews on television and in a book that Resnick's drug addiction was a possible motive for the murders.

In an interview with the picture spread, Resnick said she had started taking cocaine only two weeks before the murders after being drug-free for two years. She also said Simpson suspected his ex-wife and Goldman were secretly dating.
"He used to see them seated next to each other at Starbucks (cafe)," she said in the interview. "He always though they were having an affair.
"To my knowledge, they were just friends," Resnick said. "I know she thought he was quite handsome and he thought she was very beautiful, but as far as I know there was nothing but friendship."
If the jury decides Simpson was responsible for the murders, they must also determine compensatory damages to be awarded to Goldman's family. The Brown family are not asking for compensatory damages.
A second phase of the trial, expected to last one or two days, would then follow to help the jury determine if Simpson should pay punitive damages to both families to punish him for his actions.
